tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint for Scale Modeling
tips.text: For most scale modeling tasks, Vallejo's Acrylic and Airbrush colors are recommended. They offer a wide range of colors, excellent pigment density, and easy application with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. Use Vallejo Model Color for hand brushing, Model Air for airbrushing, and Game Color for wargaming figures. Avoid enamels like Tamiya Acrylic Paints for airbrushing due to their slow drying time.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits
tips.text: Start with 240 grit sandpaper for smoothing seams and filling putty. Progress to 320 grit for removing scratches and preparing surfaces for paint. Finish with 400 grit for a smooth, glass-like finish before applying decals. Always wet sand to avoid clogging and use a sanding block for even pressure. After sanding, clean the surface with isopropyl alcohol to remove dust.

tips.title: Filling Gaps: Tamiya Putty vs Vallejo Plastic Putty
tips.text: For small gaps and scratches, use Tamiya's Extra Thin Cement mixed with baking soda to create a lightweight filler. Apply with a fine brush, let dry, then sand smooth with 240 grit. For larger gaps, use Vallejo Plastic Putty. Apply with a palette knife, let dry, sand with 120 grit, then 240 grit before painting. Avoid using super glue alone as it shrinks and doesn't sand well.

tips.title: Photo-Etch vs Resin Detail Parts
tips.text: Photo-etch (PE) details from Eduard, Eduard's Brassin, or Arma Hobby provide excellent surface details like hinges, ladders, and tool sets. They require careful cutting, bending, and gluing with super glue. Resin details from brands like Clear Prop Models offer complex shapes like engines, landing gear, or figures. They're easier to use but often require sanding and cleaning. Choose PE for thin, delicate details and resin for bulky, complex shapes.

tips.title: Decal Setting Solutions: Micro Set/Sol vs Mr. Mark Softer
tips.text: Micro Set/Sol from Microscale is a popular decal setting solution used worldwide. Apply Micro Set with a fine brush to the decal placement area, let it soak in, then apply Micro Sol. Gently wipe off excess with a damp cloth. Let dry completely before painting. Mr. Mark Softer is a Japanese alternative that works similarly but may have a slightly different scent. Both products require careful application to avoid oversaturation or residue.
